This review is based on 100% completion and 262.3 hours of gameplay.

[h1][b]Recommendation:[/b][/h1]
Would I recommend this game? Yes, I would, but only for the multiplayer. If you want to play through the [i]Mass Effect[/i] story, go with the Legendary Edition instead of this version. Unfortunately, this is not the best PC port, and it is also where I think [i]Mass Effect’s[/i] story really started to fall off, especially towards the end. A lot of other people felt the same way too, even after the changes they made following the backlash. That said, for what it is, I still really like this game and absolutely adore this IP.

The EA launcher is required to run the game and, as always, it is annoying. There is also an issue where the game sometimes does not recognise the licence and refuses to launch. I ran into this after uninstalling and reinstalling the game. There is a simple fix on Reddit that worked for me. Here is the [b][i][url= https://www.reddit.com/r/MECoOp/comments/189u76r/mass_effect_3_product_key_could_not_activate/] Link. [/url][/i][/b]

The main reason to get this game, in my opinion, is purely for the multiplayer, which is still fairly active even now and is genuinely a lot of fun. If you want the campaign experience, you are much better off playing the Legendary Edition, which gives you all three games and all the DLC in one package. On top of that, this series has the very cool feature of importing your character from previous games, so I would strongly recommend not playing this unless you have already played and finished the original [i]Mass Effect 1[/i] and [i]2[/i]. Some story options will be locked off if you have not made certain choices in those earlier games. Also worth noting, save files from the Legendary Edition versions of [i]Mass Effect 1[/i] and [i]2[/i] cannot be used with this version, and vice versa.

There are a few important things to be aware of before going in. For some reason, this game has no controller support on PC at all, so you are stuck with keyboard and mouse unless you install mods. That is not the end of the world, but for a game like this it is definitely annoying. I have not used the controller mods myself, so I cannot comment on how well they work, but they are out there if you want to look into them.

There are also a number of bugs, mainly in multiplayer. These include invisible enemies, objectives failing to appear when they are supposed to, and the weapon scroll arrows disappearing in the menu. None of these are the worst bugs in the world, but they are still irritating and worth knowing about. I also had occasional issues where the game would launch with no audio, though restarting fixed that for me. Another weird one was that if I clicked too quickly on the main menu after loading in, it would sometimes crash the game, so give it a second before doing anything.

One thing I was genuinely happy to see was that the multiplayer is still active enough that finding games through quick match was not too difficult. You will usually want to leave your map and enemy settings on random to give yourself the best chance of finding a lobby, but it was nice to see there is still a small dedicated player base keeping it alive. That said, connections can be a bit rough depending on who you match with. Some games can be very laggy, and you may end up rubber-banding all over the place, which obviously makes things harder. This will vary depending on your distance from the host. One small tip if that starts happening: jump into cover for a second, as it can sometimes help the game sync up again. Another annoying multiplayer issue is that if someone leaves, or you back out too quickly after a match, the credits you just earned can sometimes disappear.

Just touching on the other parts of the game quickly, the narrative here is definitely the weakest of the trilogy. Even after the post-launch changes, I still do not think it lands particularly well. If you are importing your character from the previous games, there are some nice moments and changes that reflect your earlier choices, which is always good to see, but the ending is still a let-down. It is very much an “all roads lead to the same place” kind of ending. Also, the slow walking and running sections are incredibly frustrating. If you know, you know. On the other hand, the romance arcs are still done really well and are as gripping as ever, especially for my girl Tali.

The graphics and overall design are outdated, sure, but I still think they hold up well. There are some cool armour sets to collect and use, each with different buffs depending on your build. And honestly, just being back on the Normandy feels great. The audio is good overall, aside from the occasional no-audio startup bug I mentioned earlier. The voice acting is top notch, and the music complements the experience really well.

As for the gameplay, I think it is fine overall. It is fun putting together your own build and deciding whether you want to focus more on powers or weapons. For me, the biggest let-down is still the complete lack of controller support. For a game that was clearly built with consoles in mind, not having that on PC is wild. The game is still perfectly playable with keyboard and mouse, but I do think the experience would have been better with a controller.

Overall, I would only recommend getting this version for the multiplayer. If you want the campaign, go with the Legendary Edition instead, as it gives you the complete experience with all DLC in one place. Since this is an older game, I would also strongly recommend waiting for a deep sale.

[h1][b]Achievements:[/b][/h1]
Two playthroughs are required for 100% if you are not importing a character from [i]Mass Effect 2[/i]. If you are importing a character from [i]Mass Effect 2[/i], then only one run is needed. Also, the kill and class-specific achievements can mostly be done in multiplayer, so you are free to play the campaign however you like.

The achievements are all pretty easy and fairly standard. Nothing is especially difficult, but there are quite a few missables, so it is worth checking those beforehand. As long as you are thorough and keep an eye on what can be missed, you should not have any real problems.
